He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] in the class of 2022. ==Early life and high school career== Livingston was born and raised in [[Akron, Ohio]].{{cite web |last1=Thamel |first1=Pete |author-link=Pete Thamel |title=Meet Chris Livingston, the 14-year-old hoops prodigy LeBron James went out of his way to see |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/meet-chris-livingston-14-year-old-hoops-prodigy-lebron-james-went-way-see-013721817.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=July 28, 2018}} He started playing competitive basketball at age five.{{cite web |last1=Beaven |first1=Michael |title=Freshman star Chris Livingston continues to develop alongside brother Cordell as Buchtel prepares for state tournament |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20190320/boys-basketball-freshman-star-chris-livingston-continues-to-develop-alongside-brother-cordell-as-buchtel-prepares-for-state-tournament |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=March 20, 2019}} As a freshman, he played for [[Buchtel Community Learning Center]] in Akron, averaging 24.7 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game. Livingston led his team to its first state final four appearance since 1997 and became the highest scoring freshman in school history.{{cite web |last1=Goul |first1=Matt |title=Buchtel, Chris Livingston and Co. still learning after state final four run: 2019 preseason basketball tour |url=https://www.cleveland.com/highschoolsports/2019/11/buchtel-chris-livingston-and-co-still-learning-after-state-final-four-run-2019-preseason-basketball-tour.html |website=[[The Plain Dealer]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=November 20, 2019}} For his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Western Reserve Academy]] in [[Hudson, Ohio]].{{cite web |last1=Beaven |first1=Michael |title=Twin brothers Chris Livingston and Cordell Livingston transfer to Western Reserve Academy |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20191129/twin-brothers-chris-livingston-and-cordell-livingston-transfer-to-western-reserve-academy |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=November 29, 2019}} In his season finale, Livingston recorded 50 points, 20 rebounds, eight steals and five blocks in a 76–65 win over [[Bristol High School (Bristolville, Ohio)|Bristol High School]].{{cite web |last1=Beaven |first1=Michael |title=High school notebook: WRA's Chris Livingston ends season with 50 points in win over Bristol |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20200224/high-school-notebook-wrarsquos-chris-livingston-ends-season-with-50-points-in-win-over-bristol |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=February 24, 2020}} As a sophomore, he averaged 32.5 points, 12.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.9 steals and 1.4 blocks per game, earning [[MaxPreps]] Sophomore All-American first team honors.{{cite web |last1=Helwagen |first1=Steve |title=National top-five prospect Livingston hearing from key schools |url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/Article/Ohio-high-school-basketball-prospect-Chris-Livingston-2022-hearing-from-Michigan-Wolverines-Ohio-State-Buckeyes-Kentucky-Wildcats-Texas-Longhorns-148225084/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=June 15, 2020}} For the 2020–2021 season, Livingston transferred back to Buchtel to play his junior year. ===Recruiting=== Livingston was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. He held multiple college basketball scholarship offers before entering high school. Livingston was offered by [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] at age 14.{{cite web |last1=Goul |first1=Matt |title=See Chris Livingston, nationally ranked freshman in Akron and Ohio State basketball target |url=https://www.cleveland.com/hssports/blog/2018/10/see_chris_livingston_nationall.html |website=[[The Plain Dealer]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=October 2, 2018}} On September 15, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2022}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Chris Livingston | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Akron, Ohio|Akron, OH]] | highschool = [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] (VA) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 200 | 40 = | commitdate = September 15, 2021 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 92 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2022 | rivals ref title = Kentucky 2022 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2022 Kentucky Wildcats Recruiting Class | rivals school = kentucky | scout s = | espn schoolid = 96 | 247 overall = 16 | rivals overall = 11 | espn overall = 12 | accessdate = March 25, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==National team career== Livingston played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in [[Belém]], Brazil. He led his team to the gold medal, recording 23 points, six rebounds and two assists in a 94–77 win over [[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Canada]] in the final.{{cite web |last1=Beaven |first1=Michael |title=Buchtel's Chris Livingston leads USA Basketball to 2019 FIBA Americas Men's U16 title in Brazil |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20190610/buchtels-chris-livingston-leads-usa-basketball-to-2019-fiba-americas-mens-u16-title-in-brazil |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=June 10, 2019}} Livingston was named tournament [[most valuable player]] and made the all-tournament team.{{cite web |last1=Helwagen |first1=Steve |title=Buchtel's Livingston brings home
